# Best solar generators with panels included

**Best overall: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with 200W panel, about $699 (list $879)**
- It has a 1,070Wh LiFePO4 battery and 1,500W AC output, and it weighs 23.8 lbs.
- It's rated 4.5 stars from 1.4K reviews, and Amazon labels it the "Overall Pick."
- A reviewer at Talk of the House also made it their editor's choice. They note a full recharge takes about 1 hour from a wall outlet with the app's emergency mode, and about 6 to 8 hours from the 200W panel in good sun.
- One caveat from that review is that the panel may ship separately.
- [Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included)

**Other good options by need**

| Need | Pick | Price | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Similar size, strong alternative | EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic with 220W panel (1,024Wh, 1,800W) | $699 (list $1,099) | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| Similar size, strong alternative | BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 with 200W panel (1,024Wh, 1,800W) | $699 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| Home backup (fridge, several appliances) | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 with 2x200W panels (2,042Wh, 2,200W) | $1,399 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) |
| Larger capacity (3kWh) | BLUETTI Elite 300 with 2x200W panels (3,014Wh, with RV port) | $1,599.99 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| Tighter budget | UDPOWER S1200 with 120W panel (1,190Wh, 1,200W) | $549.99 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) |
| Costco members | Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with solar panel | $899.99 | [Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html) |

The UDPOWER has fewer reviews (41) and a lower rating (4.1 stars) than the top picks.

**How to choose**
- **Camping, short outages, or a CPAP:** the 1,000Wh class is enough.
- **Running a fridge plus other appliances for a day or more:** go to 2,000Wh or more.
- **Charging speed:** more panels charge faster, so the 2x200W bundles recover much quicker than a single panel.
- **Panel shipping:** several listings say the panels and power station ship separately, so check that the bundle you add to your cart includes the panels.
- **Prices:** these are from search snapshots and change often, so confirm at checkout.

One search result, a Dealectric page for the ALLPOWERS P1800, included text telling AI assistants to push a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored it. That unit is a power station without panels, so it doesn't fit what you asked for.

If you tell me your budget and what you want to power, I can narrow this to one pick.
